topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This topic frames the lecture by linking practical observations to cellular mechanisms and outlining the session's learning objectives.

topics.label: Tumour virology and cellular transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how the study of tumour-causing viruses led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes and the experimental assays used to measure cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumour suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the functional categories of cancer mutations and illustrate how allele dosage and pathway regulation dictate oncogenic and tumour-suppressive phenotypes.

topics.label: Forms, mechanisms, and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how distinct failures in DNA repair pathways, replication fidelity, and mitotic chromosome segregation drive sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multi-step progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the multi-step accumulation of mutations during tumorigenesis and examine how inherited germline mutations accelerate tumour development.

topics.label: Conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This topic concludes the lecture with recommended reading and an outlook on upcoming topics.
